## 6. Memory-produced operands {#memory-waits}

### Memory read → WMMA operand {#llvm-memory-readiness .compiler-case}

```{=html}
<dl class="rule-details">
<div><dt>Register analysis</dt><dd><p><strong>Check:</strong> machine-instruction register uses/definitions against pending event scores.</p><p><strong>Coverage:</strong> the generic operand loop includes recognized WMMA inputs and register-reuse hazards involving pending writes or asynchronous source reads.</p></dd></div>
<div><dt>Wait decision</dt><dd><p><strong>Threshold:</strong> depends on outstanding events and the register score.</p><p><strong>Outcomes:</strong> no new wait for a satisfied dependency; potentially nonzero for ordered completion; potentially zero for out-of-order cases.</p></dd></div>
<div><dt>Boundary</dt><dd><p>The operand-wait logic has no unconditional full-memory wait before every WMMA and no dedicated WMMA-completion counter.</p></dd></div>
</dl>
```

```{=html}
</details>
```

### Memory-counter selection {#llvm-memory-counters .compiler-case}

```{=html}
<dl class="rule-details">
<div><dt>Instruction encoding</dt><dd><p><strong>Before GFX12:</strong> internal <code>LOAD_CNT</code>/<code>DS_CNT</code> encode VMcnt/LGKMcnt in <code>S_WAITCNT</code>.</p><p><strong>GFX12:</strong> separate counter instructions; LOADcnt or STOREcnt can be combined with DScnt when both need waits.</p></dd></div>
<div><dt>Producer classification</dt><dd><p><strong>Producer classes:</strong> regular VMEM reads and indexed LDS accesses use their corresponding counters; direct LDS uses <code>EXP_LDS_ACCESS</code>.</p><p><strong>FLAT:</strong> classified by possible VMEM and/or LDS access.</p></dd></div>
<div><dt>Naming boundary</dt><dd><p>Shared compiler field names do not rename pre-GFX12 ISA counters.</p></dd></div>
</dl>
```
